title: A request, from input to response
summary: A small example of how to explain a code flow.
audience: A developer new to this code

files.purpose: Accept a message, clean it and return a reply.
files.details: This is a fictional teaching example. It does not contact a service.

chapters.title: Follow one message
chapters.summary: Start with what arrives and what the user gets back.

items.title: Clean
items.text: Remove spaces from the beginning and end.

items.title: Reply
items.text: Put the cleaned message in a reply object.

blocks.title: A small example
blocks.text: If the message is ' hello ', the reply contains 'hello'. Only the surrounding spaces are removed.

narration.label: The incoming message
narration.text: A caller sends a message. The request handler receives it. We will follow that message through three small steps.

narration.label: An example
narration.text: For example, a message with spaces around hello becomes hello without those surrounding spaces.

chapters.title: Read the important lines
chapters.summary: Read what each line does before worrying about its syntax.

blocks.title: The request handler
blocks.explanation: The function receives a message, asks normalize to clean it, then returns the result.

blocks.title: The helper
blocks.explanation: strip removes spaces at the beginning and end. It does not remove spaces inside the message.

narration.label: Receive the input
narration.text: This function receives the message as its input.

narration.label: Call the helper
narration.text: This line passes the message to the cleaning helper. The cleaned value is stored for the next line.

narration.label: Return the reply
narration.text: The next line returns the cleaned value inside a reply object.

narration.label: Remove surrounding spaces
narration.text: Inside the helper, strip removes only the surrounding spaces. This is the final step in our example.

quiz.question: Where are the surrounding spaces removed?
quiz.explanation: normalize calls strip to remove the surrounding spaces.
